newsitem.title: USA: R.J. Reynolds shares tobacco's view on Fla. case.
newsitem.headline: R.J. Reynolds shares tobacco's view on Fla. case.

text.p: An attorney for R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co said Friday he shared the view of lawyers for other tobacco companies that a tobacco settlement would not stop a landmark class action suit against the industry in Florida.

Reynolds attorney Hugh Whiting said he agreed with Philip Morris Cos Inc attorney David Hardy, who quoted Philip Morris as saying a settlement in the tobacco talks would not keep the suit, Norma Broin vs. Philip Morris, from going forward.
"I have no reason to have any different view of that than Mr. Hardy does," Whiting said.
Lawyers for Lorillard Tobacco Co, a unit of Loews Corp, and Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp, a unit of B.A.T Industries Plc, expressed the same view.
R.J. Reynolds is a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.
In the Broin suit, non-smoking flight attendants are suing the tobacco industry over illnesses allegedly linked to second-hand smoke.

This morning, amid speculation that a sweeping tobacco settlement was imminent, Stanley and Susan Rosenblatt, lawyers who represent the flight attendants in the class action suit, reiterated their request that Circuit Judge Robert Kaye declare that the suit will go forward, with or without a settlement in the tobacco talks.
Kaye did not issue an order but said he had concerns about whether he, a judge in state court, would have any authority to declare a federal settlement inapplicable to the Broin suit.
"Authority is the issue. I just don't know what authority I would have," Kaye said.
